composition.serve_who: Drawing GMMS 108’-114a, titled BILGE SYSTEM, primarily serves the main bilge pump, five electrically actuated bilge-valve branches, and six compartment bilge switches. Evidence is the named MAIN BILGE PUMP feed at the top, the five repeated valve/relay/terminal groups aligned with main-panel selections LAZARETTE, AFT, ENG. ROOM, FWD and SAIL LOCKER, and the field BILGE SW endpoints. The lower MAIN PANEL/PC CARD regions provide shared command, alarm and open/closed indication infrastructure; the XA11 line is an ONYX remote command to the pump loop, while XA40/XA10 are status taps per the established engineer walk.

equipment_groups.equipment_name: Main Bilge Pump — Gianneschi ACB 431 B
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: The top load is explicitly labeled MAIN BILGE PUMP, and the authoritative mapping assigns BILGE PUMP to 520-main-bilge-pump. The established engineer walk for this exact drawing identifies the local, main-panel and ONYX paths as alternative activations of one pump control loop.

functions.label: Run the main bilge pump from local, main-panel, or ONYX demand
functions.what_it_does: Supplies the pump motor and closes its solenoid contactor when any one of the three drawn/established command paths requests pumping.

flow_scenarios.path: +24 V service-battery supply → fuse F3 60 A → SW8/main contact remains open because the solenoid contactor coil is not energised → MAIN BILGE PUMP motor de-energised → chassis/negative return.

+24 V control supply → local pump switch → T/S S control lines 12/14/15 → contactor-coil terminals 13/14 close the solenoid-operated main contact → protected motor feed through fuse F3 60 A and SW8/contact → MAIN BILGE PUMP → chassis/negative return.

MAIN PANEL bilge-pump switch S13 → Plug C pins 7/6 → drawn pump control wiring and T/S S control lines 12/14/15 → contactor-coil terminals 13/14 → solenoid main contact closes → +24 V service supply through fuse F3 60 A → MAIN BILGE PUMP → chassis/negative return.

ONYX remote command at XA11:32 → cable/conductor 7 → T/S C terminal 50 → relay Re6 via fused terminal T/S B:13 → pump control wiring to contactor-coil terminals 13/14 → solenoid main contact closes → +24 V service supply through fuse F3 60 A → MAIN BILGE PUMP → chassis/negative return.

local pump switch

main-panel pump switch S13 through Plug C pins 7/6

remote-command relay Re6 through built-in replaceable fuse at T/S B:13

equipment_groups.equipment_name: Five Burkert electrically actuated bilge valves
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: The centre of the sheet contains five repeated loads labeled BILGE VALVE, each with an actuator motor, OPEN/CLOSE contacts, one relay branch, and one main-panel location selection. Established equipment identity is five Burkert rotary actuators on DN050 two-way ball valves.

functions.label: Select and isolate the bilge suction location
functions.what_it_does: Opens the selected compartment valve for pumping and closes/de-selects the branch when it is not selected, using one relay and actuator branch per location.

flow_scenarios.path: +24 V bilge-valve control supply → breaker Q13 10 A shown on this sheet → relay bank Re1–Re5 not commanded → actuator motor pairs at T/S C 9/10, 18/19, 26/27, 34/35 and 42/43 remain unpowered → valves retain their last/normal position; open/closed limit contacts remain available to indication circuits.

Main-panel S20 LAZARETTE BILGE → Plug C pin 1 → branch wiring → relay Re1 through built-in replaceable fuse T/S B:8 → T/S C actuator terminals 9/10 → lazarette-associated valve actuator → control return; OPEN/CLOSED limits return through T/S C 7/8 → Plug D pins 1/2 → main-panel PC-card lamps.

Removal of S20 selection → Re1 changes to the close drive path through fused terminal T/S B:8 → T/S C 9/10 → valve actuator to closed limit → return; closed status returns through T/S C 8 → Plug D pin 2 → LAZARETTE BILGE closed lamp.

Main-panel S21 AFT BILGE → Plug C pin 2 → relay Re2 through built-in replaceable fuse T/S B:9 → T/S C actuator terminals 18/19 → aft valve actuator → return; OPEN/CLOSED limits through T/S C 16/17 → Plug D pins 3/4 → PC-card lamps.
Removal of S21 selection → Re2 close-drive path through fused terminal T/S B:9 → T/S C 18/19 → actuator to closed limit → return; closed status through T/S C 17 → Plug D pin 4.

Main-panel S22 ENG. ROOM BILGE → Plug C pin 3 → relay Re3 through built-in replaceable fuse T/S B:10 → T/S C actuator terminals 26/27 → engine-room valve actuator → return; OPEN/CLOSED limits through T/S C 24/25 → Plug D pins 5/6.
Removal of S22 selection → Re3 close-drive path through fused terminal T/S B:10 → T/S C 26/27 → actuator to closed limit → return; closed status through T/S C 25 → Plug D pin 6.

Main-panel S23 FWD BILGE → Plug C pin 4 → relay Re4 through built-in replaceable fuse T/S B:11 → T/S C actuator terminals 34/35 → forward valve actuator → return; OPEN/CLOSED limits through T/S C 32/33 → Plug D pins 7/8.
Removal of S23 selection → Re4 close-drive path through fused terminal T/S B:11 → T/S C 34/35 → actuator to closed limit → return; closed status through T/S C 33 → Plug D pin 8.

Main-panel S24 SAIL LOCKER → Plug C pin 5 → relay Re5 through built-in replaceable fuse T/S B:12 → T/S C actuator terminals 42/43 → sail-locker valve actuator → return; OPEN/CLOSED limits through T/S C 40/41 → Plug D pins 9/10.
Removal of S24 selection → Re5 close-drive path through fused terminal T/S B:12 → T/S C 42/43 → actuator to closed limit → return; closed status through T/S C 41 → Plug D pin 10.

functions.label: Show each valve open or closed at the main panel
functions.what_it_does: Returns each actuator’s two end-position contacts to dedicated open and closed lamps, allowing the operator to verify the selected suction path.

flow_scenarios.path: Actuator not on either end limit → both dedicated position-return circuits inactive → respective OPEN and CLOSED lamps on the main-panel PC card remain unproved.

Valve OPEN limit contact → location pair at T/S C 7, 16, 24, 32 or 40 → Plug D odd pin 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9 → corresponding OPEN lamp → common +24 V lamp rail/return; the five open lines also connect through the drawn diode network to Plug D line 11.
Valve CLOSED limit contact → location pair at T/S C 8, 17, 25, 33 or 41 → Plug D even pin 2, 4, 6, 8 or 10 → corresponding CLOSED lamp → common +24 V lamp rail/return.

The register’s fitting bilge-level-sensor node is used for these detection devices; the sheet does not itself establish manufacturer/model.

functions.label: Detect compartment bilge level and issue the associated bilge demand/alarm
functions.what_it_does: Changes the compartment input circuit when a bilge switch operates, feeding the common valve/pump control and main-panel pedestal alarm wiring for the affected bilge zone.

flow_scenarios.path: +24 V sensor/control supply → compartment BILGE SW circuit remains in its normal contact state → no new zone demand through the associated T/S C field group → valve/pump demand and pedestal alarm remain inactive except for any independent manual or ONYX command.

flow_scenarios.state: Port or starboard lazarette bilge switch operated
flow_scenarios.path: PORT or STBD LAZARETTE BILGE switch → drawn field conductors through T/S C 12–15 → lazarette branch control/relay wiring → corresponding valve/pump demand path → main-panel/pedestal alarm interface; exact port-versus-starboard conductor assignment within 12–15 is not printed clearly enough to split further.
AFT BILGE switch → T/S C field group 20–23 → Re2/aft branch control wiring → aft valve and common pump-demand loop → Plug C/PC-card pedestal alarm interface and return.
ENG. ROOM BILGE switch → T/S C field group 28–31 → Re3/engine-room branch control wiring → engine-room valve and common pump-demand loop → alarm interface and return.
FWD BILGE switch → T/S C field group 36–39 → Re4/forward branch control wiring → forward valve and common pump-demand loop → alarm interface and return.
SAIL LOCKER BILGE switch → T/S C field group 44–47 → Re5/sail-locker branch control wiring → sail-locker valve and common pump-demand loop → alarm interface and return.

Active bilge alarm input → Plug C pins 8/9 and ALARM MOD drives pedestal alarm/indicator → operator mute contact through Plug C pin 11 to common Plug C pin 12 suppresses the audible output while the drawn alarm/indicator circuit remains connected.

infrastructure.system_name: Vessel Control Panel — bilge command, alarm and indication section
facts: MAIN PANEL switches S20–S24 select the lazarette, aft, engine-room, forward and sail-locker bilge branches through Plug C pins 1–5.
MAIN PANEL switch S13 commands the main bilge pump through Plug C pins 7/6; all pump activation alternatives belong to one pump loop.
Plug C pins 8–12 interface the pedestal alarm module, alarm indicator and mute contact through the four-pin AUX PLUG ON PC BOARD.
Plug D pins 1–10 carry five open/closed valve-position pairs to the MAIN PANEL PC CARD; odd pins are open and even pins are closed.
The PC card has a common +24 V indicator-lamp rail; open lines 1/3/5/7/9 also feed a five-diode network terminating at line 11, whose downstream purpose is not identified on this sheet.

infrastructure.system_name: 24 V DC service distribution feeding the bilge sheet
facts: The left vertical source is labeled +24 V SERVICE BAT.
A 200 A fuse F2 is drawn in the incoming/common supply section.
The main bilge-pump motor branch is protected on this drawing by fuse F3 60 A.
The bilge-valve control branch is protected on this drawing by breaker Q13 10 A.
Terminal strips T/S B and T/S C, relay-bank supply topology, and shared conductors are panel/distribution infrastructure rather than separate equipment.

infrastructure.system_name: ONYX Monitoring & Control — remote bilge interface
facts: The line labeled to ONYX is a distinct off-sheet monitoring/control interface.
Per the established engineer walk, XA11:32 is an activation command entering the main-pump loop through T/S C terminal 50, relay Re6 and fused terminal T/S B:13.
Per the established engineer walk, XA40:14/:12/:16 and XA10:06/:04/:02 are status taps out of the bilge circuits, not additional independent valve-command systems.

infrastructure.system_name: Bilge & Fire System — shared bilge control topology
facts: The drawing coordinates one main bilge pump, five electrically actuated suction-selection branches and six bilge switches under the titled BILGE SYSTEM.

A compartment demand uses the associated valve branch and the shared main-pump demand/alarm logic; the drawing does not depict hydraulic pipework, so no fluid connection beyond this electrical coordination is asserted.
The pedestal alarm/mute and main-panel position indications are shared system functions rather than separate pumps or valves.
